questions.prompt: What does JSX compile to?
options: HTML strings inserted with innerHTML
Native Web Components
ES template literals
Function calls that create React elements
questions.explanation: JSX is syntax sugar; a compiler turns each tag into a call that creates a React element object.

questions.prompt: Which hook adds local state to a function component?
options: useRef
useState
useMemo
useContext
questions.explanation: useState returns the current state value and a setter function.

questions.prompt: How does a parent component pass data to a child component?
options: Through props
Through the child's internal state
Through DOM events only
By calling the child's lifecycle methods
questions.explanation: Props are the inputs a parent supplies to a child as attributes in JSX.

questions.prompt: Why must each item of a rendered list (e.g. from map) have a key?
options: Keys are used as CSS class names
Keys make the items clickable
Keys prevent the list from being re-rendered at all
Keys help React identify which items were added, removed or reordered between renders
questions.explanation: Stable keys let React match old and new elements correctly during reconciliation.

questions.prompt: Why must a React component name start with a capital letter?
options: Lowercase names are reserved for hooks
JSX treats lowercase tags as built-in DOM elements and capitalised ones as components
Capital letters make the component render faster
Babel refuses to compile lowercase function names
questions.explanation: <div /> refers to a DOM element, while <Div /> refers to a component in scope.

questions.prompt: Which JSX correctly attaches a click handler named handleClick?
options: <button onclick="handleClick()">
<button click={handleClick}>
<button onClick={handleClick}>
<button @click={handleClick}>
questions.explanation: React uses camelCase event props and expects a function reference inside curly braces.

questions.prompt: What does calling a state setter such as setCount(5) do?
options: Reloads the whole page
Immediately changes the local count variable in the running function
Schedules a re-render of the component with the new state value
Replaces the component's props
questions.explanation: State updates are queued; the component re-renders and the next render sees the new value.

questions.prompt: What does useEffect(fn, []) do?
options: Runs fn after every render
Runs fn before the first render
Runs fn after the first render, and runs the returned cleanup on unmount
Runs fn only when props change
questions.explanation: An empty dependency array means the effect has no reactive dependencies, so it runs on mount only (twice in dev under Strict Mode).

questions.prompt: count is 0. A click handler runs setCount(count + 1) three times in a row. What is count after the re-render?
options: It throws an error
questions.explanation: Each call reads the same stale count of 0 from that render; use setCount(c => c + 1) to accumulate updates.

questions.prompt: Why does calling items.push(x) and then setItems(items) usually fail to update the UI?
options: push is not allowed on arrays held in state variables
setItems only accepts functions
React clones the array so push has no effect
React sees the same array reference and treats the state as unchanged
questions.explanation: State updates are compared by reference with Object.is, so state should be replaced with a new array.

questions.prompt: What should an effect that starts a setInterval return?
options: A cleanup function that calls clearInterval
The interval id as a number
Nothing; React clears intervals itself
A promise that resolves when the interval ends
questions.explanation: The returned function runs before the effect re-runs and on unmount, preventing leaked timers.

questions.prompt: Two sibling components need to read and change the same piece of state. Where should the state live?
options: In a module-level variable that each sibling mutates
In each sibling, synchronised with useEffect
In their nearest common parent, passed down as props
In a ref inside one of the siblings
questions.explanation: Lifting state up to the closest shared ancestor keeps a single source of truth.

questions.prompt: What makes an input a controlled component?
options: It is wrapped in a form element
It has a ref attached to it
It uses defaultValue instead of value
Its value is driven by React state and an onChange handler updates that state
questions.explanation: In a controlled input, the displayed value always comes from state.

questions.prompt: What happens when you assign to ref.current of a useRef ref?
options: The value changes but the component does not re-render
The component re-renders immediately
The change is lost on the next render
React throws because refs are read-only
questions.explanation: Refs are mutable containers that persist across renders without triggering updates.

questions.prompt: A child wrapped in React.memo still re-renders every time. The parent passes style={{ color: "red" }}. Why?
options: React.memo ignores props that are objects
A new object is created on each parent render, so the shallow prop comparison fails
style props always bypass memoisation
memo only works on class components
questions.explanation: Inline object literals have a new identity each render; memoise the object or define it outside the component.

questions.prompt: How does useLayoutEffect differ from useEffect?
options: It runs on the server during rendering
It runs only once, before the first render
It runs after the browser has painted
It runs synchronously after DOM mutations but before the browser paints
questions.explanation: useLayoutEffect blocks painting, which is useful for measuring layout, while useEffect usually runs after paint.

questions.prompt: A reorderable list of inputs uses the array index as each item's key. What problem can occur after reordering?
options: State and DOM of each input stay with the position rather than the item
React throws a duplicate-key error
The list stops re-rendering
Every item is unmounted and remounted
questions.explanation: With index keys, React reuses the component at each position, so internal state sticks to the wrong item.

questions.prompt: Why must hooks be called in the same order on every render?
options: Hooks are stored by variable name
Hooks must run in alphabetical order
React matches hook state to calls by their position in the call order
Calling them out of order is a syntax error
questions.explanation: Hook state is kept in an ordered list per component, so conditional calls would shift the mapping.

questions.prompt: Why does React call component functions twice in development under Strict Mode?
options: To warm up the JIT compiler
To help surface impure rendering and effects that lack proper cleanup
To render each component on the server and on the client
Because production also renders twice
questions.explanation: Double-invoking render and mounting effects exposes side effects that violate React's purity expectations; it is dev-only.

questions.prompt: What does wrapping a state update in startTransition tell React?
options: The update must run before any other update
The update should run on a background thread
The update should be skipped if it is slow
The update is non-urgent and can be interrupted by more urgent updates such as typing
questions.explanation: Transitions let React keep the UI responsive by prioritising urgent updates and rendering the non-urgent update in an interruptible way.

questions.prompt: A Context Provider is given value={{ user, theme }} written inline. What is the effect?
options: Every parent render creates a new object, re-rendering all consumers even if user and theme are unchanged
Consumers never re-render
Only consumers that read theme re-render
React automatically memoises the value
questions.explanation: Context compares the value by reference, so a new object identity triggers consumer updates; memoise it with useMemo.
